title: Keyset pagination over an org's user directory
name: User directory listing

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code paginates through an organization's users? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: There is none. The query orders by (created_at DESC, id DESC), a total order because id is unique, and the cursor predicate uses the same tuple with a row-value comparison `(created_at, id) < (...)`, so users sharing a created_at are neither skipped nor repeated. Fetching limit + 1 rows detects whether another page exists without an extra count, nextCursor is built from the last returned row, limit is clamped, the cursor is validated, and all values go through bind parameters. One thing that looks risky but is fine: created_at is emitted with toISOString, which has millisecond precision, so it only round-trips exactly if the column stores milliseconds; it is otherwise correct for typical timestamp usage here.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does the query request limit + 1 rows?
choices: To include the cursor row itself so the client can confirm continuity
To know whether another page exists without running a separate COUNT query
To compensate for rows filtered out by the status condition after fetching
Because Postgres LIMIT is exclusive of its bound
choiceQuestions.explanation: If more than limit rows come back, hasMore is true, the extra row is dropped, and a nextCursor is issued; otherwise nextCursor is null. The predicate is strict '<', so the cursor row is not included; status filtering happens in SQL, not afterwards; and LIMIT n returns up to n rows.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A new user is inserted into the org while a client is halfway through paging. Assuming created_at is the insertion time, what does the client see?
choices: The new user appears on the next page, shifting every later row by one
A user from the previous page is repeated on the next page
Pages already fetched are unaffected and the new user does not appear in the remaining pages
The cursor becomes invalid and the next request fails
choiceQuestions.explanation: Ordering is newest first and the next page only asks for rows strictly older than the cursor. A newly created user is newer than the cursor, so it falls before it and is not returned in later pages, and nothing shifts. Offset pagination would cause the duplicate/shift; the cursor stays valid because it encodes values, not positions.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A client sends a cursor that is valid base64url but decodes to {"createdAt":"x"}. What happens in listUsers?
choices: The cursor is ignored and the first page is returned
The query runs with a null id and returns nothing
Postgres raises a cast error that propagates to the caller
choiceQuestions.explanation: The decoded value is an object, not a two-element array, so the shape check throws InvalidCursorError (and the catch rethrows it as InvalidCursorError too). The cursor is not silently ignored and the query is never executed, so no Postgres error occurs.
